summary: Full frontend smoke of ERP 3.0 suite (21 vendor pages + admin ERP settings). Vendor login, ERP Hub (20 tiles), Product Master (localStorage save/edit), Purchase Book with Owner Lock Gate, Inventory KPIs, Business Profile, Learning Center (13 tiles + article view), Roles (4 system roles), Security (password change form), Reports (Generate/PDF/Excel/CSV), GST Assistant 5-line summary, and all 10 owner-gated pages all render correctly. Admin login → /admin/erp-settings loads with 5 tabs (GST slabs, HSN mapping, Thresholds, Reminders, Learning content), all switch, Save button present, sidebar entry visible. VendorNav shows ERP 3.0 link. No blocking JS errors — only expected 404s from /api/erp/* (Preview mode banners shown as designed) and one benign React hydration warning.

issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' in the GST% <select> around ErpProducts.jsx line 271. The GST_SLABS map renders `<option value={g}>{g}%</option>` — build-time instrumentation wraps the {g}% expression in a <span>, which is not valid inside <option>. Non-blocking but pollutes console. Fix: render the option text as a plain template string, e.g. `<option value={g}>{`${g}%`}</option>` or `{g + '%'}`, so no child span is emitted.

action_items: Optional: fix the <span> inside <option> hydration warning in /app/frontend/src/pages/vendor/erp/ErpProducts.jsx (GST_SLABS mapping around line 271) to keep console clean.
critical_code_review_comments: OwnerLockGate treats ANY non-404 error as failed verify but pass-through on 404 is correct per spec. Once backend ships, ensure /api/erp/owner-security/verify returns 401/200 explicitly; today the gate accepts any password because the endpoint 404s — this is by design per user's Preview mode fallback but MUST be revisited before production.
listProducts / listPurchases fallback to localStorage even on non-404 errors (5xx, network) — could silently mask real failures. Consider surfacing a toast on non-404 errors.
erp.js file is ~250 lines and mixes many concerns; consider splitting into products/purchases/dashboards/admin modules as backend endpoints stabilise.
